chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'I heard Rabi'at al-Ra'y saying: When she sees blood from the third menstruation, she is irrevocably divorced from him, and the period is only what is between the two menstruations,' and he claimed that he took this by his own opinion. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'He lied! By my life, he did not say that by his own opinion, but he took it from Ali (peace be upon him).'

He (the narrator) said, 'I said to him, 'And what did Ali (peace be upon him) say regarding it?'' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He (peace be upon him) used to say: When she sees blood from the third menstruation, her waiting period has ended, and there is no way for him upon her, and the period is only what is between the two menstruations, and it is not for her to marry until she performs the ritual bath from the third menstruation.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on triple divorce and the waiting period?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the Shia jurisprudential principle that a woman becomes irrevocably divorced (mubarrqa) after the third menstruation, a ruling attributed directly to Imam Ali rather than being mere personal opinion (ra'y). It specifies that while the waiting period (iddah) concludes with the third bleed, she must perform the ritual bath (ghusl) before she is permitted to remarry, distinguishing between the end of the waiting period and the finality of the bond.
